chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn Sadaqah from Salih al-Nili who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'One who visits the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him), acknowledging his right, Allah records for him the reward of freeing one thousand slaves, and like the reward of one who carried one thousand saddled and bridled horses in the way of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) emphasizes that the spiritual merit of Ziyarat al-Husayn is contingent upon *‘irfan* (gnostic recognition) of the Imam’s divine station, not merely physical presence. By equating this visitation with freeing a thousand slaves or equipping a thousand fully saddled warhorses, the text highlights the immense, cumulative reward for those who understand the theological significance of Karbala within Shia cosmology.
